blocks.title: Key Takeaways
items: Serves as a transitional phase connecting the Paleolithic and Neolithic ages.
Microliths—small, finely made stone tools used for arrowheads, spear points, and sickles—were the defining technology.
Lifestyles shifted toward fishing alongside hunting, with early temporary settlements developing near rivers and lakes.
Art evolved with more detailed cave paintings where human figures became more prominent.
Major historical sites include Bhimbetka (Madhya Pradesh) and Bagor (Rajasthan).

blocks.content: The Mesolithic Age lasted roughly from 10,000 BC to 6,000 BC.
The Mesolithic Age represents a transitional phase between the Paleolithic and Neolithic ages.
The Mesolithic Age represents a transitional phase between the Paleolithic and Neolithic ages. - Humans still hunted animals
but began to adopt more efficient techniques. - This period shows early signs of settlement near water sources.

items: The most important tools were microliths, which were very small and finely made stone tools.
These tools were often used as arrowheads, spear points, and sickles. One-liner for SSC: Microliths belong to the Mesolithic Age.
People hunted animals and also started fishing.
Temporary settlements developed near rivers and lakes.
Microliths belong specifically to the Mesolithic Age (frequently asked in SSC exams).
Important site locations often tested: Bhimbetka is located in Madhya Pradesh and Bagor is in Rajasthan.
The Mesolithic Age marks the earliest signs of human settlement near water sources and the introduction of fishing.
Cave paintings continued but became more detailed.
